title: Physiological effects in humans induced by the visual stimulation of room interiors with different wood quantities

findings.antecedent: Room with 45% wood ratio
findings.mechanism: Assumed appropriate and moderate wood quantity led to higher comfort.
findings.quote: The 45% room tended to be evaluated as the most comfortable.

findings.antecedent: Room type (0%, 45%, 90% wood ratio)
findings.mechanism: Visual characteristics of wood influence perception of naturalness.
findings.quote: The main effect of the room type on the natural feeling was significant in one-way ANOVA (Table 1)

findings.antecedent: Room with 45% wood ratio compared to 0% wood ratio
findings.mechanism: Presence of wood materials enhances perceived naturalness.
findings.quote: there were significant differences (P < 0.05) between the 0% and 45% rooms

findings.antecedent: Room with 90% wood ratio compared to 0% wood ratio
findings.mechanism: Presence of wood materials enhances perceived naturalness.
findings.quote: and between the 0% and 90% rooms.

findings.antecedent: Room type (0%, 45%, 90% wood ratio)
findings.quote: No significant difference was observed in the restful feeling

findings.antecedent: Room type (0%, 45%, 90% wood ratio)
findings.quote: There was no significant difference between the three rooms.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 0% wood ratio room interior (19s to 31s exposure)
findings.mechanism: Autonomic nervous activity (parasympathetic dominance) leading to stress reduction.
findings.quote: Diastolic blood pressure decreased significantly after 19s to 31s and stayed below the baseline.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 0% wood ratio room interior
findings.quote: the pulse rate of the subjects did not change for the entire exposure.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 0% wood ratio room interior
findings.quote: Similarly, systolic blood pressure did not show a significant change.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 45% wood ratio room interior (16s to 31s and 45s to 53s exposure)
findings.mechanism: Autonomic nervous activity (parasympathetic dominance) leading to stress reduction.
findings.quote: A significant decrease in the diastolic blood pressure was observed between 16 and 31s, and between 45 and 53s.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 45% wood ratio room interior (after 54s exposure)
findings.mechanism: Possible compensation for the decrease in blood pressure.
findings.quote: The pulse rate in the 45% room gradually increased after the subjects opened their eyes, and the increase became significant after 54s.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 45% wood ratio room interior
findings.quote: The trend in the systolic blood pressure was similar to the diastolic blood pressure, but no significant difference was observed.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 90% wood ratio room interior (from approximately 20s exposure)
findings.mechanism: Autonomic nervous activity (parasympathetic dominance) leading to stress reduction.
findings.quote: Both systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure showed a significant and large decrease from approximately 20s

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 90% wood ratio room interior (from approximately 17s exposure)
findings.mechanism: Autonomic nervous activity (parasympathetic dominance) leading to stress reduction.
findings.quote: diastolic blood pressure from 17s), which was interpreted to mean that the parasympathetic nervous activity was dominant

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 90% wood ratio room interior (after 81s exposure)
findings.mechanism: Possible compensation or fatigue due to excessive stimulation.
findings.quote: The pulse rate did not change significantly, except for a sudden increase after 81s.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 0% wood ratio room interior (after initial 10s exposure)
findings.consequent: Total hemoglobin concentration [tHb] in right prefrontal lobe
findings.mechanism: Increased regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) and cerebral activity, possibly due to interest in the interior design.
findings.quote: the [tHb] changed little during the initial 10s of the exposure, but tended to increase afterward to reach a significant increase.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 45% wood ratio room interior (latter part of exposure)
findings.consequent: Total hemoglobin concentration [tHb] in right prefrontal lobe
findings.mechanism: Increased regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) and cerebral activity, possibly due to interest in the interior design.
findings.quote: The [tHb] tended to increase especially in the latter part of the exposure in the 45% room.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 90% wood ratio room interior (42s to 81s exposure)
findings.consequent: Total hemoglobin concentration [tHb] in right prefrontal lobe
findings.mechanism: Increased regional cerebral blood flow (rCBF) and cerebral activity, possibly due to interest in the interior design.
findings.quote: In the 90% room, a significant increase in the [tHb] was observed intermittently between 42 and 81s

findings.antecedent: Visual stimulation of 90% wood ratio room interior (last 10s exposure)
findings.consequent: Total hemoglobin concentration [tHb] in right prefrontal lobe
findings.mechanism: Subjects became tired of the large coverage of wood and gave up information collection, leading to decreased cerebral activity.
findings.quote: but the [tHb] showed a sudden drop in the last 10s.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimuli of room interiors with different wood quantities (0%, 45%, 90%)
findings.quote: In the present study, diastolic blood pressure decreased significantly in all three rooms with different wood quantities.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimuli of room interiors with 45% or 90% wood quantities
findings.mechanism: Autonomic nervous activity, possibly as compensation or due to fatigue.
findings.quote: However, the pulse rate increased significantly in the 45% room, systolic blood pressure significantly decreased in the 90% room, and these two indices were unchanged in the 0% room.

findings.antecedent: Visual stimuli of room interiors with 90% wood quantity
findings.quote: However, the pulse rate increased significantly in the 45% room, systolic blood pressure significantly decreased in the 90% room, and these two indices were unchanged in the 0% room.

stimuli.description: Three actual-size model rooms (13 m²) with varying wood ratios: 0% (white carpet, white wallpaper), 45% (wooden floor, waist-high wooden wall), and 90% (almost all wall/floor/ceiling covered with sliced oak veneer).

tables.description: Results of one-way analysis of variance on 'natural' feeling in rooms with different wood ratios

limitations: Studies addressing physiological mechanisms and individual differences are required to explain the implication of the physiological responses.
